label: check060
claim: 701 kN axial load and FE-normalized reliability walls correct the carbon table; the no-float screen survives.
source_report_body: CHECK MAINLINE-060 filed, QUESTIONABLE/PROJECTION. Owner code not read or run; rebuilt from 051, 052, 054 and the primary PDFs. The answer stands: no carbon frame floats on sourced compression; not a better lead than SiC. 216 of 237 checked numbers reproduce. Confirmed: DIALEAD K13D2U 340 MPa and the 340-380 MPa pitch set, GRANOC, M55J 890, NCAMP CV 5.198 and CMH-17's 6%; the 0 deg ratio 1.7875 and 0.190 GPa first ply (my lamination theory on 051's plies); every whole-bill row within 1 kg (M55J -469.9 at R10); the CV 6% Pf walls; hail 28.5-32.3 J against Kim's 254 J (Pernas-Sanchez's scaling gives 250 J at 1.45 mm). Mismatches: the member load is 701 kN axial (158 klb, 1.30x NG-2), not 775 kN (1.43x); the Pf walls multiply 051's FE-normalized k(m) by a 0.5-0.8% lower peak (M55J 70/10/10/10 x1.326 not x1.316, R10 -2,092 not -2,044 kg); every CV 5.2% column runs about 1% high (conservative); M55J hail stress 98.9 not 100 MPa. m = 1.2/CV is conservative by 3-4% in m. Objections: Montagnier and Hochard blame their 15% gap on premature Celanese ruptures, so it is not an independent shortfall; Messinger's 110K strut fittings (27.8%, nearer the 158 klb load) leave even the strength-ignored light frame sinking (R10 -730, R30 -11,661 kg). Nine NFI. Next: none.
numerical_scope: Synthesis of attributed reports; consult named check/review findings for numerical disposition
qualification: Neither is a global impossibility proof. The corrected hypothetical TRL7 row is not achieved maturity; rejected carbon cases do not qualify SiC. [CHECK057](unpublished-local-ref:68eae3652d6c0a12), [CHECK060](unpublished-local-ref:d8968524247a969e).
